name: GameAgenda Local-First PWA (static Steam snapshot + micro edge API)
one_liner: An installable SvelteKit PWA where searching all ~196.6k Steam games and every write happen on the device: a sub-millisecond prefix index runs in a Web Worker and writes go to IndexedDB optimistically. A daily static catalog snapshot feeds it. A GitHub Actions job builds that snapshot from Steam and publishes it free on Cloudflare. The only server code is a stateless Worker called on demand (game details, unknown appids, optional Steam import), plus optional sync later.

components.name: PWA app (apps/web)
components.responsibility: Screens: Agenda (tabs per Estado, flag filters, counters), Apuntar overlay (per-keystroke search, quick add, paste link/appid, manual title-only add, undo toast), Explorar (virtual list of the WHOLE Steam catalog: popularity, A-Z, year; +18 hidden), Ficha (detail sheet), Ajustes (export/import, covers on/off, +18 toggle, storage status, perf panel). Keeps the agenda in memory (Svelte $state) and applies every change optimistically before persisting. All routes are prerendered at build time as static shells with no user data, then hydrated, and data loads client-side.
components.tech: SvelteKit 3.1.0 (adapter-static 4.0.0, config inside sveltekit() in vite.config.ts) + Svelte 5.57.3 runes, Vite 8.3.5, TypeScript 6.0.3

components.name: Service Worker
components.responsibility: Precaches the hashed app shell cache-first (lists from $app/manifest, version from $app/env), so restarts need no network. Caches Steam covers at runtime (cache-first, CORS mode, LRU of 400, skipped when 'Cargar portadas' is off or Save-Data is on). Serves an offline navigation fallback and activates new versions on the next launch.
components.tech: SvelteKit 3 bundled module service worker, Cache Storage

components.name: Search Worker
components.responsibility: Owns the catalog lifecycle: manifest check at most every 12 h, core download, delta chain, sha256 check, storage in CacheStorage, atomic swap. Builds the prefix index and answers {q, seq} with ranked rows. Also serves Explorar pages, appid lookups and details-shard fetches. It never touches user data.
components.tech: Dedicated module Web Worker, typed arrays + bitsets, CacheStorage (exposed in workers), code from packages/core

components.name: Local store
components.responsibility: Persists entries (Steam and manual games), settings and an append-only change log with per-field HLC stamps. The log drives undo, import merge and future sync. Also handles export/import JSON and calls navigator.storage.persist().
components.tech: Dexie 4.4.7 over IndexedDB, crypto.randomUUID ids, ~40-line HLC from packages/core

components.name: Shared core library (packages/core)
components.responsibility: One implementation, tested once, used by the browser worker, the pipeline and the edge: accent folding/tokenizing, roman-numeral aliases, core/delta TSV codecs, shard hashing, ranking, Steam link parser, HLC + LWW merge, entry schema validation.
components.tech: TypeScript 6.0.3 with erasableSyntaxOnly (runs unbuilt on Node 24 type stripping), Vitest 5.0.5

components.name: Catalog pipeline (packages/catalog-pipeline)
components.responsibility: Runs three modes: daily delta, weekly reconcile and a one-off backfill. GetAppList (key) provides the authoritative list and GetItems (keyless, best-effort) the enrichment. Then it classifies, applies validation gates, emits manifest/core/deltas/details shards, deploys, saves state and writes a run summary.
components.tech: Node 24.21 scripts (built-in fetch, node:zlib brotli/gzip, node:crypto), GitHub Actions cron on ubuntu-24.04, wrangler 4.154.0, gh CLI

components.name: Catalog CDN (ga-catalog)
components.responsibility: Serves the public snapshot. /manifest.json gets max-age=300. Content-hashed files under /v/ (core, deltas, details shards, shard index) get max-age=31536000, immutable. Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is set via _headers. About 1,050 files per version.
components.tech: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets, assets-only Worker on workers.dev (custom subdomain later), Free plan

components.name: Edge API (/api/v1/* on ga-web)
components.responsibility: The smallest unavoidable server piece, never on the hot path. /items calls GetItems for appids missing from the snapshot or with stale covers. /details/:appid returns trimmed Spanish appdetails, edge-cached 24 h. From M5, /steam/resolve, /library, /wishlist and /achievements are pass-through only (no storage, Cache-Control no-store). Holds the Steam key as a secret, validates inputs strictly, calls only a fixed upstream allowlist and allows CORS only from the app origin.
components.tech: Cloudflare Worker with static assets (run_worker_first ['/api/*'], not_found_handling single-page-application) + Hono 4.13.14, Cache API, wrangler secret

components.name: Pipeline state
components.responsibility: master.ndjson.gz holds every field the pipeline needs (base/es names, type, flags, dates, reviews, cover paths, last_modified, price_change_number, enrichedAt) plus the delta cursor. 14 dated copies are kept for rollback. If the state is missing, the pipeline rebuilds from scratch (~990 calls).
components.tech: GitHub Release asset 'catalog-state' (gh release download / upload --clobber)

components.name: Steam (external)
components.responsibility: List: IStoreService/GetAppList/v1 (key in the x-webapi-key header). Enrichment: IStoreBrowseService/GetItems (keyless). On demand: appdetails. M5: GetOwnedGames (key), IWishlistService/GetWishlist, IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements + GetGameAchievements (keyless) and profile ?xml=1. Covers are hotlinked from shared.akamai.steamstatic.com.
components.tech: api.steampowered.com, store.steampowered.com, steamcommunity.com; never partner.steam-api.com, never PICS or the Steam client protocol

components.name: Sync service (post-prototype)
components.responsibility: Optional multi-device sync of the change log: push/pull since a cursor, LWW per field by HLC, behind Sign in through Steam or passkeys.
components.tech: Same Worker + Cloudflare D1 (Free: 5M rows read/day), steam-signin 1.0.5

components.name: QA and performance harness
components.responsibility: Unit tests for core logic and a 100-query golden ranking set. Playwright E2E (add flow, offline, share route) on Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. A perf project with CDP CPU throttling asserts the budgets. CI has size gates (JS <= 90 KB brotli, core <= 3 MiB brotli) and a grep that fails if the Steam key leaks into build output.

stack.why: Already installed. Runs the pipeline's .ts files directly via type stripping and has built-in fetch, zlib, crypto and --env-file. Node 26 (Active LTS from today) is an optional later bump.

stack.choice: pnpm workspaces, installed with npm -g (not corepack)
stack.why: Fast, strict monorepo: apps/web, apps/edge, packages/core, packages/catalog-pipeline. Node 25+ no longer ships corepack, so a global install keeps working after a Node upgrade.

stack.choice: TypeScript, one version for the whole repo
stack.why: SvelteKit 3.1 peer-requires ^6 and svelte-check needs the TS API. TS 7.0.2 has no API until 7.1, so switch then.

stack.choice: SvelteKit (static output, every route prerendered, client-side data) + Svelte 5 runes
stack.why: Smallest runtime of the listed options, which helps first-visit LCP on phones. Fine-grained reactivity suits per-keystroke result updates. Kit bundles a module service worker from the build manifest. Output is purely static.
Required by Kit 3 (>= 8.0.12). Fast on Windows. Module Web Workers work via new URL(..., import.meta.url).
Schema versioning, unique and multi-entry indexes, bulk operations and transactions with little code. Works in every target browser.

stack.choice: Custom word-prefix index + bitsets + substring fallback in a module Web Worker (packages/core)
stack.why: Measured 0-0.3 ms/query with ~16 MiB retained. FlexSearch, Orama and MiniSearch use 67-316 MB of heap, Fuse.js takes ~394 ms, and SQLite FTS5 trigram needs a 19.2 MiB DB (11.5 MiB brotli).

stack.choice: Web App Manifest (share_target, shortcuts) + the SvelteKit 3 service worker ($app/manifest, $app/env, $app/paths)
stack.why: No PWA plugin to keep compatible. The precache list comes straight from the build.

stack.choice: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets (ga-web shell, ga-catalog snapshot)
stack.why: Free, unlimited static requests with no egress fees. 25 MiB per file, 20k files per version, _headers for CORS and caching, edge locations in Spain.
Smallest possible server piece: stateless, secrets via wrangler secret, Cache API. The free 10 ms CPU and 100k requests/day are ample because it is off the hot path.

stack.choice: GitHub Actions cron + workflow_dispatch; state kept as a GitHub Release asset
stack.why: Free, with no extra service or card. Best-effort timing is acceptable because runs are cursor-based and idempotent.
One fast tool for TS, JSON and CSS, with no dependency on the TS API.

stack.choice: Vitest (unit tests, golden search set) + Playwright (E2E, performance, offline)
stack.why: Vitest is Vite-native. Playwright gives CPU throttling via CDP and runs WebKit on Windows, which matters with no Mac.
Typed bindings for the API Worker.
The only sign-in Valve offers third parties, verified server-side in the Worker.
Same Worker and account. A SQL change log is enough for personal lists.

catalog_pipeline:
SOURCES
1. Authoritative list (documented, keyed). GET https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?include_games=true&include_dlc=false&include_software=false&include_videos=false&include_hardware=false&max_results=50000[&last_appid=N][&if_modified_since=T]
   - The key goes only in the x-webapi-key header. It is the GitHub secret STEAM_WEBAPI_KEY and never appears in URLs or logs. Never use partner.steam-api.com.
   - Page with have_more_results/last_appid; results come in ascending appid order.
   - The full list is about 196.6k games (about 133.9k released + 62.7k coming soon, including free and adult games), which takes 4 calls. DLC (about 63.9k) is deliberately excluded.
   - Delisted games are not returned and deletions are never reported, which is why a weekly reconcile exists.
2. Enrichment (undocumented, keyless, best-effort). GET https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1/?input_json=...
   - Up to 200 ids per call, so the URL stays under ~8 KB.
   - context {language:'spanish', country_code:'ES'}. The country is mandatory or the reply comes back empty.
   - data_request {include_assets, include_release, include_platforms, include_reviews}, with include_best_purchase_option=false. Never use include_extra_details in bulk.
   - Fields kept:
     - type: only 0 (game) enters the core; 1 demo, 4 DLC and 11 music are dropped
     - localized name, is_coming_soon, is_early_access
     - release: steam_release_date, coming_soon_display, custom_release_date_message
     - unlisted
     - content_descriptorids: 3 or 4 means adult
     - reviews: review_count, percent_positive, review_score
     - assets: asset_url_format + library_capsule, with header as fallback
     - platforms + steam_deck_compat_category
   - success 15 + appid 0 means the app does not exist: drop it.
   - success 15 + unvailable_for_country_restriction means region-locked in ES: keep it, flag it, and re-query those ids with country_code 'US'.
3. Dev and bootstrap only. The jsnli/steamappidlist daily dump is used as a fixture; it has no license, so it never goes to production. If the key arrives late, a keyless listing is possible via IStoreQueryService/Query (1000 items/call, sort=2, about 197 calls; region-locked titles drop out).

SCHEDULE
.github/workflows/catalog.yml: cron '17 3 * * *' plus workflow_dispatch(mode); concurrency group 'catalog'; 90-minute timeout; ubuntu-24.04; Node 24.21.
- daily (default):
  - GetAppList with if_modified_since = cursor − 3600 s: 1 call, about 3.3k changed games/day.
  - Then GetItems for changed and new appids, plus a rolling slice: floor(appid/10) mod 28 = day of cycle, about 7k games, so every game is re-enriched every 4 weeks.
  - Total about 10.3k ids, or about 52 calls.
- reconcile (Sundays, or more than 7 days since the last one):
  - Full GetAppList (4 calls).
  - Appids that vanished get one GetItems pass: unlisted → keep with a 'Retirado' flag (ranked low, still addable); nonexistent → remove; region-locked → keep.
- backfill (no state found): 4 + about 983 calls. State is checkpointed every 100 calls, so a cancelled run resumes.
- Missed runs are harmless. The cursor is the highest last_modified already applied, so the next run just gets a bigger delta.
- Rate control: one worker, token bucket at 0.4 req/s (about 120 per 5 min, never above 1 req/s), 20 s timeout, 5 retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and a global pause on HTTP 429 (60 s, doubling up to 10 min).

EMIT
All output comes from pure, deterministic functions in packages/core: the same input gives the same bytes and therefore the same hashes.
- /v/core.<seq>.<sha8>.txt
  - Served as text/plain; charset=utf-8, so Cloudflare compresses it on the fly.
  - Header line '#ga-core 1 <seq> <count>', then one TAB-separated line per game, sorted by appid: appidDelta, name, flagsHex, year, pop[, esName].
  - flags: comingSoon | earlyAccess | adult | delisted | regionLockedES | hasCover.
  - year = release year − 1970 (0 = TBA).
  - pop = round(10·log2(review_count+1)), range 0-255.
  - esName only when the Spanish name differs (about 0.5% of old games, about 4% of new ones).
  - Size: the measured appid+name TSV is 1.80 MiB brotli; the target is about 2.0 MiB brotli and 5-6 MB raw.
- /v/delta.<from>-<to>.<sha8>.txt
  - '+<full line with absolute appid>' upserts and '-<appid>' removals.
  - Expected 20-60 KB/day compressed. The last 14 are kept.
- /v/d/<shard>.<sha8>.json
  - shard = fnv1a32(appid) mod 1024. Appids are mostly multiples of 10, so a plain modulo would leave buckets empty.
  - Rows: [appid, coverPath, headerPath, releaseDay, comingSoonText, reviewScore, reviewCount, percentPositive, platformBits, deckCategory].
  - About 192 games per shard, about 10 KB compressed.
  - Unchanged shards keep their hash, so clients keep them cached.
- /v/details-index.<seq>.<sha8>.json: the 1024 shard hashes, about 6 KB.
- /manifest.json: {schema:1, seq, builtAt, games, enrichmentAgeDays, core{url,bytes,sha256}, deltas[{from,to,url,bytes}], details{shards:1024, index}}.
- Cover path:
  - asset_url_format with ${FILENAME} replaced by assets.library_capsule; header is the fallback, and apps with no assets get no cover.
  - Legacy hash-less filenames are never synthesized.
  - The client prefixes https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/.
- _headers (rules do not overlap, so header values never get concatenated):
  - '/*' → Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  - '/v/*' → Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
  - '/manifest.json' → Cache-Control: public, max-age=300

VALIDATE → PUBLISH → SAVE
- Gates:
  - at least 190k games, and within −2%/+5% of the previous run
  - at most 1% of names changed
  - sentinel appids present: 10, 220, 620, 730, 413150, 1145360, 1245620
  - every line parses and appids strictly ascend
  - core at most 3 MiB brotli
  - shards pass schema validation
- If a gate fails:
  - nothing is published, and clients keep the last snapshot
  - the job fails and GitHub e-mails the owner
  - the job opens or updates an issue 'Catálogo: fallo del pipeline'
- An enrichment failure is not a pipeline failure. GetAppList names are still published with the last-known enrichment, and enrichmentAgeDays grows.
- Publish:
  - wrangler deploy of the assets-only ga-catalog Worker. Only changed hashes upload, each version is atomic, and there are about 1,050 files against the 20,000 limit (largest about 6 MB against 25 MiB).
  - A client holding an old manifest that hits a 404 refetches the manifest and retries.
- Save:
  - gh release upload catalog-state master.ndjson.gz --clobber, plus a dated copy (14 kept).
  - Counts, calls, bytes and durations go to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
- Rollback: rerun with --mode=publish --state=<date>.

CALL BUDGET
- Backfill, once: 4 keyed + about 983 keyless calls. That is about 41 min at 0.4 req/s and about 250 MB downloaded.
- Steady state: about 1 keyed + 52 keyless calls per day (2-3 min of calls, a job of about 4 min), plus 4 keyed calls per week.
- That is about 5 keyed calls/day against the 100,000/day ToU cap.
- If GetItems volume ever matters, input_protobuf_encoded batches of about 700 ids cut calls about 3.5x.

LATER SOURCES
- IGDB can become a second source in the same job:
  - backend only, 4 req/s, 8 concurrent, caching encouraged, visible attribution
  - maps Steam appids through external_games source 1
  - adds game_time_to_beats
  - the core gains a source column
- GetTagList (446 Spanish tags, version_hash) and GetStoreCategories (72) can feed filters.
search_design:
PRINCIPLE
The whole catalog is searched on the device, offline, with no search library.

EVIDENCE (measured on this PC, Node 24, 196.6k names)
- Simple word-prefix inverted index: 0-0.3 ms/query (220-330 ms build, ~16 MiB retained).
- Brute-force substring scan: 7-14 ms median.
- uFuzzy: ~5 ms/keystroke (28 MB peak).
- Fuse.js: ~394 ms.
- FlexSearch / Orama / MiniSearch: 67-316 MB heap.
- SQLite FTS5 trigram: 0.14-0.45 ms, but a 19.2 MiB DB (11.5 MiB brotli).
- Chosen: a custom prefix index plus a substring fallback.
- Remote Steam search rejected: 250-380 ms per query, mixes in DLC and soundtracks, no CORS.

NORMALIZATION (packages/core; identical in the worker, the pipeline and the tests)
- fold(s):
  1. NFKD.
  2. Strip \p{M}: removes accents, ñ becomes n.
  3. Lowercase.
  4. Remove ™ ® © and apostrophes (Assassin's → assassins).
  5. Turn every other non-letter/digit into a space and collapse spaces.
- Pure-ASCII names (91.9%) take a lowercase-only fast path.
- compact(s) = fold(s) without spaces, so 'halflife' and 'cs2' match.
- Display uses the original string:
  - TM symbols are kept.
  - The 18 empty names show as '(sin nombre) · #appid'.
  - Long names (up to 542 B) are ellipsized.

TOKENS
- The base name and the Spanish name are both folded and split on whitespace.
- Roman↔digit alias tokens for i-x after the first word, so 'Hades II' ↔ 'hades 2'.
- CJK/Hangul names (6.3%) stay as whole tokens; the substring stage finds them.

INDEX (built in the Search Worker from the core text; double-buffered on updates)
- Game ids are assigned in static-rank order: pop desc → released before coming soon → shorter name → lower appid. In M1, before pop exists, the order is released, then shorter name, then lower appid.
- terms: a sorted array of unique tokens. offsets and postings are Uint32Arrays, with ids ascending, so the best rank comes first.
- exactTitle: a Map from folded full title to ids, so exact titles always surface even when obscure.
- Bitsets of N bits (about 6.2k words, 24 KB each):
  - adult, comingSoon, delisted
  - 36 precomputed first-character unions for one-letter queries
- Explorar permutations (A-Z, year) as Uint32Array.
- Footprint about 20-30 MB in the worker. Build takes about 0.3 s here, estimated 1-1.5 s on a mid-range phone.

QUERY (each keystroke posts {q, seq}; the latest wins; no debounce)
1. A Steam link or appid pattern → binary search on appids → an exact card pinned first.
2. Tokens of fold(q):
   - Each token → binary search for its prefix range in terms → OR its postings into a scratch bitset (a one-letter token uses its precomputed bitset).
   - AND across tokens.
   - AND-NOT adult unless 'Mostrar +18' is on.
3. Walk the set bits from id 0 upward (best rank first) and stop at 200 candidates. Rescore:
   - exact title +1000
   - title starts with the query +400
   - first token matched +100
   - tokens in order +50
   - plus pop
   - minus coming soon and delisted
   Return the top 30 as {appid, label, esLabel, year, flags}.
4. Stage 2 runs only when there are fewer than 10 hits and the query has at least 3 characters (or the input is CJK):
   - a compact-substring scan in rank order with a 15 ms time slice
   - sent as a second message, so stage 1 is never delayed
   - it covers mid-word queries
5. Matching agenda entries, manual games included, appear first under 'En tu agenda' (max 3). They are searched on the UI thread, which is fine for a few thousand titles.

COST
Typically under 1 ms here. Worst case (1-2 letters) is a union of up to 600k postings: about 2-3 ms here, an estimated 10-15 ms or less on a mid-range phone.

READINESS
- Stage A (core lines parsed; estimated 0.3-0.6 s on a phone) enables the brute-force path.
- Stage B (index built) enables the prefix path.
- Before stage A, manual add and link paste already work and the bar shows 'Cargando catálogo… x%'.

LISTING ('listar todos los juegos')
- Explorar is a virtual list: 56 px rows, about 20 DOM nodes, 100 rows per worker RPC.
- Sorts: popularity (default), A-Z, year.
- Filters via bitsets: Lanzados / Próximamente / Todos, and +18.
- The total is shown, e.g. '196.595 juegos'.

QUALITY
- A Vitest golden set of 100 typical queries from Spanish users:
  - 'elden' → ELDEN RING
  - 'hades 2' → Hades II
  - 'the witcher 3'
  - accent-insensitive 'mision' → 'Misión…'
- From M2: top-1 at least 90%.
- Later, only if needed:
  - uFuzzy for typo suggestions when there are 0 results
  - a persisted typed-array index
  - FTS5 trigram via sqlite-wasm 3.54.1 if substring needs grow
  - GetTagList-based filters
capture_flow:
TARGET
From intent to saved in under 3 s, one-handed, online or offline, with no confirmation dialogs.

ENTRY POINTS
- Agenda always shows a pinned 'Apuntar un juego…' bar. One tap opens the full-screen Apuntar overlay with the keyboard up. On desktop, '/' or Ctrl+K works from anywhere.
- Android and desktop Chromium with the PWA installed:
  - a manifest shortcut 'Apuntar juego' (/?apuntar=1) opens with focus
  - the Web Share Target (GET /share?title&text&url) means 'Compartir → GameAgenda' from the Steam app or any browser adds the game directly
- iOS has no share target (iOS 26 opens Home Screen sites as web apps):
  - copy the Steam link, open the app, tap the 'Pegar enlace' chip (clipboard read on a user gesture)
  - no Shortcuts 'Open URL' recipe: it would open Safari, whose storage is separate from the Home Screen app

STEAM GAME (default path)
1. Type 3-5 letters. Results refresh on every keystroke (≤ 50 ms) and show:
   - the name (the Spanish name when it differs, with the base name as subtitle)
   - the year
   - badges: Próximamente, Acceso anticipado, Retirado
   - 'Ya en tu agenda · Jugando' if the game is already saved
2. Tap the 48 px '+' (desktop: ↑/↓ then Enter):
   - an entry is created with status Quiero jugar and addedAt
   - the row turns into '✓ Quiero jugar' within 100 ms
   - a toast 'Añadido a Quiero jugar · Deshacer · Cambiar' shows for 5 s
3. Long-press '+' (desktop: Alt+Enter) for a one-tap picker: Jugando / Completado / Platinado / Comprado / Próximo.
4. The query text stays selected, so typing the next title replaces it. Several games can be captured in a burst.
5. In the background, the Search Worker fetches that game's details shard (~10 KB from the CDN, usually cached) and stores the cover path and release date in the entry. Offline, this is queued and retried.

Typical timing: 0.3 s tap + 1.0-1.5 s typing + ~0.5 s scan and tap ≈ 2 s.

LINK OR APPID (~1-1.5 s)
- Accepted when pasted or shared:
  - store.steampowered.com/app/<id>/<slug>
  - steamcommunity.com/app/<id>
  - s.team/a/<id>
  - steam://store/<id>
  - 'appid <n>'
- The link is parsed locally and the exact card is pinned first. Through the share target the game is added automatically, with undo.
- If the appid is not in the local snapshot (newer than the last build, or delisted before our first snapshot):
  - a provisional entry is created, titled from the URL slug ('Hades' from /app/1145360/Hades/) or 'Steam #<id>'
  - it is corrected later by /api/v1/items (M4) or by the next snapshot

MANUAL GAME (non-Steam, PlayStation, physical…)
- The last row is always 'Añadir «<texto>» como juego propio' (Enter when there are no hits).
- It creates a title-only manual entry instantly, even offline.
- An optional platform chip follows: PS5, Switch, Xbox, PC, móvil, otro.
- PlayStation 'platinado' is a manual flag.

GUARANTEES
- gameKey is unique, so there are no duplicates. For an already-saved game, the '+' becomes its status chip.
- Works before the catalog finishes loading (manual and link paths), and fully offline after the first load.
- Every change can be undone from the toast. Nothing ever asks 'are you sure?'.
user_data_and_sync:
PRINCIPLE
The device is the source of truth. The network is never on the write path.

MODEL (Dexie 4.4.7, DB 'gameagenda', schema v1)
- entries:
  - id: crypto.randomUUID
  - gameKey (unique): 'steam:<appid>' | 'manual:<uuid>' | later 'igdb:<id>'
  - source, appid?
  - title: stored in the entry; the Spanish name when available
  - coverPath?, year?
  - platforms[]: where the user plays or owns the game (steam, ps5, switch, xbox, pc-otro…)
  - status: 'quiero' (default) | 'jugando' | 'pausa' | 'completado' | 'abandonado'
  - flags: Record<string, true> for platinado, comprado, proximo. This is an open set, so new flags such as favorito or físico need no migration.
  - note
  - dates: addedAt, startedAt, completedAt, platinadoAt, compradoAt, statusChangedAt (stamped automatically, editable)
  - steam?: playtimeMin, lastPlayed (from M5)
  - hlc: one stamp per field
  - deleted?: tombstone
  - updatedAt
  - indexes: &gameKey, status, updatedAt, *flagList
- changes: ++seq, entryId, field, value, hlc, deviceId. Append-only; drives undo, import merge and the future sync push; compacted over time.
- meta: settings, deviceId, HLC clock, catalogSeq, lastExportAt, steamProfile?.

WRITE PATH
1. Tap.
2. Mutate the in-memory Svelte $state and paint (under 16 ms).
3. Run the Dexie transaction (entries + changes) off the critical path.
4. On failure (e.g. quota), revert and show a toast.

Rules:
- Platinado also sets status Completado (and completedAt) in the same change set.
- The first move to Jugando stamps startedAt.
- Próximo pins the game to the top of Quiero jugar.
- Delete writes a tombstone, with a 5 s undo toast.
- Nothing uses confirmation dialogs.

READ PATH
- All entries load at startup (1k entries is about 300 KB and takes 50 ms or less), and per-status lists are derived from them.
- Each entry keeps its own title and cover, so the agenda renders before or without the Steam catalog.

DURABILITY
- Call navigator.storage.persist() after the first add.
- Show install prompts (Android beforeinstallprompt, iOS instructions), because Safari deletes the storage of non-installed sites after 7 days without interaction.
- Export:
  - JSON 'gameagenda/v1' with full fidelity, including HLC stamps, so it can be merged back
  - CSV for spreadsheets
  - via download, or Web Share with files on mobile
- Import is an idempotent LWW merge by gameKey, run in the worker.
- While there is no sync, remind the user to export every 30 days.
- 'Borrar todo' wipes IndexedDB and the caches.

SYNC PATH (post-prototype, M6; no redesign needed)
Ids are global UUIDs, every field carries an HLC and every change is in the outbox, so sync is additive:
- POST /api/v1/sync {cursor, changes[]} on the same Worker, backed by Cloudflare D1:
  - table changes(user_id, entry_id, field, value_json, hlc, device_id, server_seq)
  - index (user_id, server_seq)
- The server stores the pushed changes and returns other devices' changes since the cursor, plus a new cursor.
- The client merges with the same LWW function used for import.
- Auth: Sign in through Steam (steam-signin 1.0.5) or passkeys, with a signed HttpOnly cookie (strictly necessary, so no banner).
- D1 Free (5M rows read/day) is far more than personal lists need.

Rejected at this scale:
- Zero, Electric and PowerSync: they need Postgres logical replication plus a sync service.
- InstantDB: closed to signups and shutting down on 2027-08-31.
- Dexie Cloud: the free tier allows 3 production users.
- Replicache: in maintenance mode.

Fallbacks if leaving Cloudflare: the Turso or Neon free tiers.
steam_account_integration:
SCOPE
Optional. The core loop never needs it: import in M5, verified login in M6.

PHASE A: no login, keyless wherever possible (M5)
1. Ajustes → 'Importar desde Steam' → paste the profile URL.
   - The client parses /profiles/<id64> itself.
   - For /id/<vanity>, it calls GET /api/v1/steam/resolve, and the Worker fetches https://steamcommunity.com/id/<vanity>/?xml=1 (keyless) to get the steamID64.
2. 'Biblioteca' → /api/v1/steam/library?steamid=…
   - The Worker calls GetOwnedGames with the key in the x-webapi-key header.
   - Parameters: include_played_free_games=true, include_appinfo=false (names come from our catalog).
   - It returns only appid, playtime_forever and rtime_last_played.
   - It needs the user's 'Detalles de juegos' privacy set to Público. If the response is empty or hidden, the app shows step-by-step Spanish guidance.
   - Exactly 1 keyed call per import.
3. 'Lista de deseados' → /api/v1/steam/wishlist, using IWishlistService/GetWishlist (keyless). Returns appids and date_added.
4. Preview screen, entirely local, grouped into 'Sin jugar', 'Jugados', 'Ya en tu agenda' and 'Deseados'. Defaults:
   - unplayed owned games → Quiero jugar + Comprado
   - played games → Comprado only (the user can promote them to Jugando or Completado)
   - wishlist → Quiero jugar
   - family-shared titles are never marked Comprado
   The selection is applied as one batch with a single undo.
5. Platinado suggestions on demand, per game (Ficha → 'Comprobar logros'):
   - uses IPlayerService/GetUserAchievements + GetGameAchievements (keyless, about 1 call per game)
   - 100% produces a suggestion '¿Marcar como Platinado?', never an automatic change
   - the Steam Achievement Sets beta (Oct 2026) changes what 100% means
6. Re-import is a manual button. It merges by gameKey with LWW and never overwrites a status the user set.

PHASE B: verified identity (M6, together with sync)
- 'Sign in through Steam' (OpenID 2.0, the only option Valve offers third parties), using steam-signin 1.0.5 in the Worker with server-side check_authentication (keyless).
- The returned SteamID64 becomes the account id. The session is a signed HttpOnly cookie.
- This stops users from importing someone else's public profile and anchors sync.
- Use Valve's official sign-in button images.

COMPLIANCE HOOKS
- Data is fetched only when that user taps the button: no polling, no background refresh.
- The Worker is a pure pass-through: Cache-Control no-store, logging off on /steam/*.
- Data is stored only on the device. 'Borrar datos de Steam' removes the profile id and playtime fields.

NEVER
Steam passwords, Steam Guard codes, session tokens, PICS or the Steam client protocol.
hosting_and_costs:
RECURRING COST
€0/month on free tiers.

- ga-web (Cloudflare Worker with Static Assets, Free):
  - Shell requests are static, so they are free and unlimited.
  - Only /api/v1/* invokes the Worker: 100k requests/day and 10 ms CPU each on the free plan. Our handlers use about 1-3 ms of CPU and at most 2 subrequests.
- ga-catalog (assets-only Worker, Free):
  - About 1,050 files per version (limit 20,000); largest file about 6 MB raw (limit 25 MiB).
  - Unlimited requests, no egress fees.
- GitHub Free (repo + Actions):
  - Daily job about 4 min including setup, about 120 min/month.
  - Weekly reconcile adds about 10 min/month; the one-off backfill takes about 50 min.
  - CI takes about 3-6 min per push.
  - A public repo has free minutes, but scheduled workflows are disabled after 60 days without activity.
  - A private repo gets about 2,000 free min/month, which covers this.
  - Recommendation: private repo.
- Steam Web API key: free. The account must be non-limited (at least US$5 spent) and use the Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator.
- Domain: optional; use workers.dev during the prototype. About €10-20/year for e.g. a .es or .app before sharing publicly; it also enables app. and catalog. subdomains.

DATA PER USER
- First visit: about 2.1-2.4 MB. The shell is at most 0.15 MB; the core is about 2.0-2.3 MB depending on the brotli level Cloudflare uses on the fly (1.80 MiB at maximum level, measured).
- Returning users: about 20-60 KB/day of deltas plus a ~1 KB manifest.
- Covers: about 50-150 KB each, served by Valve's CDN, not our bandwidth.
- Example: 10k first visits is about 23 GB, which costs $0 on static assets.

STEAM CALLS
- Backfill: about 990, once.
- Then about 53 per day plus about 4-10 per week.

WHY NOT OTHER HOSTS
- Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only.
- Netlify Free spends 15 credits per deploy, and we deploy data daily.
- Render's free tier spins down.
- Fly.io has no free tier.
- Supabase Free pauses after 7 idle days.

UPGRADE PATH
- Workers Paid at US$5/month, only if /api traffic passes 100k/day (about 5k DAU at 20 API calls per user per day; the hot path never calls it).
- D1 Free (5M rows read/day) for M6 sync.
dev_setup_on_this_machine:
REQUIREMENTS
Nothing beyond what is installed: Node 24.21, npm 11.19, git 2.56. No Docker, Python, PostgreSQL, Java, Android Studio or Mac. Tauri and Capacitor are not needed for the prototype.

1. TOOLING (PowerShell)
   - `npm i -g pnpm@12.15.0`. Use this rather than corepack, which is gone from Node 25+.
   - If PowerShell blocks the pnpm.ps1 shim, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`, or call pnpm.cmd.
   - `git config --global core.autocrlf false` and `git config --global core.longpaths true`.
   - Add a .gitattributes with `* text=auto eol=lf`.
   - Optional: a Windows Defender exclusion for the repo folder and the pnpm store speeds up installs.

2. REPO LAYOUT (pnpm workspace; pnpm-workspace.yaml: apps/*, packages/*)
   - apps/web: SvelteKit.
   - apps/edge: the Worker deployed as ga-web, with the Hono API and ../web/build as assets.
   - packages/core
   - packages/catalog-pipeline: also contains wrangler.catalog.jsonc for ga-catalog.
   - .github/workflows/ci.yml and catalog.yml
   - .gitignore: .env, .dev.vars, apps/web/static/catalog-dev/, packages/catalog-pipeline/out/.

3. SCAFFOLD AND PIN
   - `git init -b main`, then `pnpm init`.
   - `pnpm dlx sv create apps/web` (minimal template, TypeScript).
   - `pnpm -F web add -D @sveltejs/kit@3.1.0 @sveltejs/adapter-static@4.0.0 @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte@7.3.1 svelte@5.57.3 vite@8.3.5 svelte-check@4.7.7 typescript@6.0.3`
   - `pnpm -F web add dexie@4.4.7`
   - `pnpm -F edge add hono@4.13.14`
   - `pnpm -F edge add -D wrangler@4.154.0 @cloudflare/workers-types@5.20261027.1`
   - `pnpm add -Dw @biomejs/biome@2.6.3 vitest@5.0.5 @playwright/test@1.64.1 typescript@6.0.3`
   - `pnpm exec playwright install chromium webkit firefox`

4. SVELTEKIT 3 SPECIFICS
   - There is no svelte.config.js. Options go in sveltekit({...}) in vite.config.ts: adapter-static output 'build', all routes prerendered.
   - tsconfig extends $app/tsconfig, with explicit include and exclude.
   - src/service-worker gets its own tsconfig extending $app/tsconfig/service-worker.
   - $service-worker is gone. Use $app/manifest, $app/env and $app/paths. The service worker is registered as a module.

5. TYPESCRIPT FOR NODE SCRIPTS
   - Packages run unbuilt on Node 24, e.g. `node packages/catalog-pipeline/src/run.ts`.
   - tsconfig: erasableSyntaxOnly, verbatimModuleSyntax, allowImportingTsExtensions, noEmit. Imports use .ts extensions.
   - Secrets are loaded with `node --env-file=.env` (the file is gitignored).

6. CLOUDFLARE
   - Create a free account, then `pnpm -F edge exec wrangler login`.
   - apps/edge/wrangler.jsonc:
     - main: src/index.ts
     - assets: { directory: '../web/build', not_found_handling: 'single-page-application', run_worker_first: ['/api/*'] }
   - Local secret: apps/edge/.dev.vars with STEAM_WEBAPI_KEY=…
   - Production secret: `pnpm -F edge exec wrangler secret put STEAM_WEBAPI_KEY`
   - ga-catalog is an assets-only config pointing at packages/catalog-pipeline/out.

7. STEAM KEY
   - Register at steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey with domain 'localhost'. The account must be non-limited (at least US$5 spent) and use the Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator.
   - Until it is approved, `pnpm catalog:fixture` builds a dev snapshot from the jsnli/steamappidlist dump into apps/web/static/catalog-dev/.
   - .env.development sets PUBLIC_CATALOG_BASE=/catalog-dev/.

8. DAILY LOOP
   - `pnpm -F web dev`: Vite at http://localhost:5173, with server.proxy sending /api to http://localhost:8787.
   - `pnpm -F edge dev`: wrangler dev on local workerd.
   - `pnpm test`: Vitest.
   - `pnpm e2e`: Playwright, including the perf project with CPU throttling.
   - `pnpm check`: Biome and svelte-check.

9. REAL STEAM DATA LOCALLY
   - `node --env-file=.env packages/catalog-pipeline/src/run.ts --mode=backfill --out=apps/web/static/catalog-dev`
   - About 45 min the first time; after that, --mode=daily takes about 3 min.

10. PHONES
    - Android: enable USB debugging, open desktop Chrome at chrome://inspect and add a port forward for 5173. The phone opens http://localhost:5173, which is a secure context, so the service worker and install work. No Android SDK needed.
    - iPhone: use the HTTPS preview URL from `wrangler versions upload` in CI.
    - With no Mac there is no Safari Web Inspector. Use the in-app Ajustes › Rendimiento panel, plus Playwright WebKit on Windows for engine coverage.

11. GITHUB
    - Private repo.
    - Secrets: STEAM_WEBAPI_KEY, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (scoped to Workers Scripts: Edit), CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.
    - The release 'catalog-state' is created once by the first catalog run; the gh CLI is preinstalled on runners, so it is not needed locally.
    - Pin third-party actions by commit SHA.
compliance_and_security:
STEAM ToU (2010) AND API HYGIENE
- The key lives only in the GitHub Actions secret and the Worker secret.
  - It is sent only in the x-webapi-key header, never in client bundles, URLs or logs.
  - CI greps the build output for the key value and for 'x-webapi-key'.
- Only api.steampowered.com is used, never partner.steam-api.com.
- About 5 keyed calls/day against the 100,000/day limit. Keyless calls stay at or below 1 req/s, with backoff.
- A user's Steam data is fetched only when that user taps 'Importar': no polling, no background refresh.
- Never: Steam passwords or tokens, PICS, or the Steam client protocol.
- No implied endorsement:
  - 'Steam' is not in the app name or icon.
  - The About screen and footer carry the notice: 'Steam y el logotipo de Steam son marcas comerciales o marcas registradas de Valve Corporation en EE. UU. y otros países. GameAgenda no está afiliada a Valve.'
  - Valve's official 'Sign in through Steam' images are used when login arrives.

GDPR / SPAIN
- M1-M4: lists live only on the device, so we hold no account data.
  - Cloudflare processes IP addresses in transit as a processor at its global edge.
  - Hotlinked covers send the user's IP and user agent to Valve (USA). This is disclosed in the privacy notice. Images use referrerpolicy='no-referrer', and 'Cargar portadas' can be switched off.
- Only storage strictly necessary for the requested service is used: IndexedDB and CacheStorage, no cookies, no analytics. So no consent banner is needed (LSSI art. 22.2). Any future analytics or RUM is opt-in.
- M5 import:
  - SteamID64 plus owned games, playtime, wishlist and achievements are personal data. Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b).
  - Minimisation: only appid, playtime_forever, rtime_last_played and wishlist appids.
  - The Worker is a stateless pass-through: no storage, logs off for /steam/*, no-store responses.
  - Data is stored on the device.
  - A layered notice (a short text in the import dialog plus the full policy) says which Steam data is stored and where: the device, transit through Cloudflare's edge, and Valve (USA).
  - Export (JSON) and delete ('Borrar datos de Steam', 'Borrar todo').
  - Before public release, write the record of processing with the AEPD tool Facilita RGPD.
- Ages: no accounts until M6. With accounts, require users to declare they are 14 or older (the Spanish digital-consent age), configurable to 16 if the pending change passes.
- Adult titles (content descriptors 3/4) are hidden by default.
- Third-party data later:
  - IGDB with visible attribution.
  - ITAD only after asking, because its terms forbid competing apps.
  - No HLTB scraping, Giant Bomb, RAWG mirroring, SteamGridDB automation or PCGamingWiki data (NC licence).
  - PlayStation 'platinado' stays manual (no NPSSO).

SECURITY
- CSP via SvelteKit's csp option in hash mode for the prerendered pages, plus _headers:
  - default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'
  - connect-src 'self' <catalog origin> https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com
  - img-src 'self' data: https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com
  - worker-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'
- Also: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()), and HSTS once on a custom domain.
- Edge API:
  - Fixed upstream allowlist, so it is not an open proxy.
  - Validated inputs: integer appids; steamid64 of 17 digits starting 7656119; vanity matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,32}; at most 50 ids per call.
  - CORS limited to the app origin.
  - Per-isolate token bucket.
  - Responses carrying user data are never cached.
- Client:
  - All Steam strings are rendered as text (no {@html}).
  - JSON import is schema-validated and capped at 10 MB, and runs in the worker.
- Supply chain:
  - Exact version pins plus the lockfile.
  - Minimal runtime dependencies: svelte, @sveltejs/kit, dexie, hono.
  - Weekly Dependabot.
  - Actions pinned by commit SHA.
  - Least-privilege tokens: the Cloudflare token is scoped to Workers, and GITHUB_TOKEN gets contents: write only in the catalog job.
performance_plan:
Each budget is checked by measurement, in CI and on a real device.

1) KEYSTROKE → RESULTS ≤ 50 ms p95
How it is met:
- The query runs in the Search Worker on the prefix index: 0-0.3 ms/query measured on this PC. Phones are several times slower, which still leaves single-digit ms.
- No debounce; the latest seq wins.
- At most 30 rows (~3 KB) cross postMessage, and the keyed Svelte list updates at most 30 rows.
- The substring stage comes as a separate, later message.
- The input handler does no I/O.
- Until the index is built (about 1-1.5 s after start on a mid-range phone), the brute-force path answers (7-14 ms median on this PC).
How it is measured:
- A performance.mark on the 'input' event, and another after the next requestAnimationFrame following the DOM commit.
- The last 500 samples are kept and shown as p50/p95 in Ajustes › Rendimiento.
- Playwright perf project:
  - Chromium with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4 (mid-range phone) and 6 (low-end, informative only)
  - types 100 game names character by character (about 600 keystrokes)
  - asserts p95 ≤ 50 ms at 4x
- CI fails on a regression of more than 20% against main.

2) TAP → FEEDBACK ≤ 100 ms
How it is met:
- Optimistic update of in-memory state, then paint.
- The Dexie transaction (about 5-15 ms) runs after, off the critical path.
- Instant CSS :active feedback.
- Undo toast instead of dialogs.
- No network on any tap.
How it is measured:
- Event Timing API (PerformanceObserver 'event', durationThreshold 16) in Chromium.
- Playwright asserts duration < 100 ms at 4x throttle for add, status change and flag toggle.

3) INP p75 ≤ 200 ms
How it is met:
- No long tasks on the main thread. The worker handles catalog download, parsing, indexing, deltas, JSON import/export and Explorar sorting.
- Explorar is a virtual list (about 20 rows in the DOM).
- The agenda is virtualized above 200 rows, with content-visibility:auto below that.
- Image boxes have fixed sizes, so there are no layout shifts.
- Dexie bulk operations are chunked.
How it is measured:
- Lab INP from Event Timing in Playwright, plus Chrome performance traces.
- Per-session INP stored locally in the perf panel.
- Field RUM comes later and only with opt-in consent.
- iOS has no Event Timing, so rAF-based timings are used there.

4) FIRST-VISIT LCP ≤ 2.5 s
How it is met:
- Every route is prerendered to static HTML at build time (header, the 'Apuntar un juego…' bar, empty state). The LCP element is text painted from HTML and CSS before any JS runs.
- Critical CSS inlined, system font stack, inline SVG icons.
- JS budget ≤ 90 KB brotli, enforced by a CI size gate.
- No images above the fold.
- The ~2 MB catalog download starts only after 'load' (requestIdleCallback, 1 s timeout), inside the worker, so it never competes with LCP.
- Cloudflare edge with points of presence in Spain.
How it is measured:
- Lighthouse mobile preset (simulated slow 4G and 4x CPU) on every preview deployment, gated at a lab LCP ≤ 2.0 s for margin.
- Spot checks on the reference Android over mobile data.

5) CACHED RESTART ≤ 2 s
How it is met:
- The service worker serves the shell from Cache Storage, with no network.
- The agenda is read from IndexedDB (≤ 50 ms for 1k entries) and painted first.
- The worker then reads the cached core (about 50-150 ms), parses it (stage A) and builds the index (stage B) in the background.
How it is measured:
- Marks 'agenda-visible' and 'search-ready', relative to performance.timeOrigin.
- A Playwright 'second launch, offline' scenario asserts agenda-visible ≤ 1 s and search-ready ≤ 2 s at 4x.
- Real-device check at the exit of M1 and M3.
- Fallback if a phone misses the budget: persist the built typed-array index in IndexedDB, keyed by catalog seq, so it loads without a rebuild.

DEVICE MATRIX
- This PC: Chromium/Edge, Firefox, Playwright WebKit.
- One mid-range Android as the reference device for all budgets.
- One iPhone through the HTTPS preview, using the perf panel (no Mac, so no Web Inspector).

milestones.name: M0 · Cimientos y fixture
milestones.scope: pnpm workspace (apps/web, apps/edge, packages/core, packages/catalog-pipeline). SvelteKit 3.1 static shell with web manifest and service worker. Biome, Vitest and Playwright set up. CI: lint, typecheck, unit, e2e, size gates and key-leak grep, plus deploys of ga-web and ga-catalog to workers.dev. Dev snapshot built from the jsnli/steamappidlist dump. Request the Steam Web API key (domain 'localhost').
milestones.acceptance: pnpm dev works on this Windows PC and CI is green. The shell installs from https://ga-web.<subdominio>.workers.dev on Android Chrome. ga-catalog serves the fixture manifest with CORS * and the immutable /v/* header.

milestones.name: M1 · Todo Steam listable y buscable + apuntar a 'Quiero jugar'
milestones.scope: Pipeline v1 on GetAppList on the GitHub cron: backfill, daily delta via if_modified_since, weekly reconcile, gates, publish, state. Core format v1, with the flag/year/pop columns present but zero until M2. Search Worker: fold, prefix index, ranking, substring stage, two-stage readiness, CacheStorage. Apuntar overlay: per-keystroke results, '+', Enter, paste link or appid, manual title-only add, undo toast. Agenda list for 'Quiero jugar'. Explorar as a virtual list of the whole catalog. Dexie store. Offline support. Perf marks and the Playwright perf project.
milestones.acceptance: (1) The Explorar count equals manifest.games (about 196.6k) and the list scrolls to the end. (2) 200 random appids from a live GetAppList page each appear in the top 5 when their name is typed (empty names excluded). (3) Keystroke-to-results p95 is at most 50 ms in Playwright at 4x CPU and in the perf panel on the reference Android. (4) Tapping '+' shows the confirmed 'Quiero jugar' state within 100 ms; entries survive reload and airplane mode, with no duplicates. (5) First-visit LCP is at most 2.5 s (Lighthouse mobile). (6) 3 consecutive scheduled runs are green, each with at most 10 keyed calls, and the key is absent from all build output. Keep the URL private until M2 ships the adult filter.

Agenda tabs, counters and filters. GetItems enrichment stage: Spanish names, type filter, coming soon and early access, adult flag, year, popularity, cover paths. 1024 details shards. Ranking with popularity. Covers in the Agenda (hotlinked, lazy, cached by the service worker). +18 hidden by default. Golden query set.
milestones.acceptance: Every state and flag is one tap away from the Agenda and from results; Platinado sets Completado and stamps dates; undo restores exactly. Backfill uses at most 1,000 GetItems calls with 0 unhandled 429s, and daily runs stay at or below 60 keyless calls. Golden set: top-1 at least 90% and top-3 at least 98% (hades 2 finds Hades II). Titles with content descriptor 3 or 4 stay hidden until the toggle is on. At least 98% of enriched agenda entries show a cover; the rest show the header or a placeholder, never a synthesized URL.

milestones.scope: Web Share Target (/share) and manifest shortcuts. 'Pegar enlace' chip. Desktop shortcuts: /, Ctrl+K, Enter, Alt+Enter, Esc. Burst capture. Export/import JSON, plus CSV export. navigator.storage.persist(). Install prompts (Android beforeinstallprompt, iOS instructions). Client-side delta chain. Ajustes › Rendimiento panel. Ficha sheet: cover, date, platforms, Deck, reviews label, description, screenshots. Layered privacy policy, aviso legal and trademark notice. CSP and security headers.

Local preview with groups and defaults; batch apply with a single undo. Privacy notice before the first import. 'Borrar datos de Steam'.
milestones.acceptance: A public profile with about 1,000 games imports in at most 5 s using exactly 1 keyed call. A private 'Detalles de juegos' setting produces Spanish guidance. Family-shared titles are never marked Comprado. Re-import never overrides states the user set. No Steam data is stored server-side (no storage bindings, logs off on /steam/*).

milestones.name: M6 · Sync opcional (post-prototipo)
milestones.scope: Sign in through Steam (steam-signin 1.0.5, server-side check_authentication) or passkeys, with a signed HttpOnly session cookie. D1 change log and POST /api/v1/sync (push/pull since a cursor, LWW per field by HLC). Account deletion. Declaration of age 14 or older. AEPD record of processing.
milestones.acceptance: Two devices editing offline converge to the same state after sync (property-based test over random interleavings). Deleting an account removes all its server rows. Free-tier usage stays under 5% with 100 active users.

risks.risk: The Steam Web API key arrives late: the account must be non-limited (at least US$5 spent) and use the Steam Guard Mobile Authenticator.
risks.mitigation: Develop M0-M1 on the jsnli/steamappidlist fixture. If production is needed before the key, list games via the keyless IStoreQueryService/Query (about 197 calls, ES context, region-locked titles missing), then switch to GetAppList once the key arrives. Never ship the dump as a dependency.

risks.risk: The undocumented GetItems/Query endpoints change shape, need new parameters or get blocked.
risks.mitigation: Enrichment is a separate, optional stage with schema validation. On failure, keep the last-known enrichment, still publish GetAppList names, surface enrichmentAgeDays and fail loudly in CI. appdetails, fetched per game on demand through the edge, is the fallback for the Ficha.

risks.risk: Steam rate limiting or 429s, more likely from shared GitHub runner IPs.
risks.mitigation: A single worker at 0.4 req/s, exponential backoff with jitter, a global pause on 429, checkpoints and cursor-based resume. The rolling refresh spreads the load. The backfill can run once from the developer PC (node --env-file=.env ...).

risks.risk: The GitHub cron runs late, drops runs, or is disabled after 60 days without activity (public repos).
risks.mitigation: Runs are idempotent and cursor-based, so a missed day only enlarges the next delta. Also: workflow_dispatch, failure e-mails plus an automatic issue, a private repo (about 2,000 free min/month against about 150 used) and a documented manual local run. Clients cope with a stale snapshot.

risks.risk: On-device data is lost: Safari deletes non-installed sites after 7 days idle, the user clears storage, or the phone is lost.
risks.mitigation: Install prompts, navigator.storage.persist(), export/import with a 30-day reminder, an 'Instala la app' banner in iOS Safari, and sync in M6.

risks.risk: Real phones are much slower than this PC: index build time, memory, or the worker being killed in the background.
risks.mitigation: All heavy work in the worker, two-stage readiness, a reference-device check at M1 exit, a persisted typed-array index if restart misses 2 s, and results capped at 30 rows.

risks.risk: Catalog growth pushes the first download past budget.
risks.mitigation: A CI size gate (core at most 3 MiB brotli), deltas for returning users, the option to move the coming-soon and adult tail into a lazily loaded second file, and a columnar binary format v2.

risks.risk: Cloudflare free-tier terms change, or Steam blocks requests from Worker IPs.
risks.mitigation: The hot path is static files, which can move to any static host such as GitHub Pages. API features are optional and fall back to snapshot data. Workers Paid at US$5/month if the limits bite.

risks.risk: Valve objects, or ToU/trademark problems arise from a public metadata snapshot or the branding.
risks.mitigation: Minimal fields, no Valve marks in the name or icon, a trademark notice, no implied endorsement, a ToU checklist in the repo and a privacy policy. The catalog layer is source-agnostic, so IGDB (with attribution) can complement or replace Steam.

risks.risk: Search quality gaps: no popularity in M1, typos, CJK, roman numerals, delisted games missing.
risks.mitigation: Golden query set in CI, popularity from GetItems reviews in M2, roman-to-digit aliases, the compact-substring stage, and an always-visible manual add. uFuzzy only for 0-result suggestions, if needed.

risks.risk: Steam cover filenames are hashed and change, so hotlinked images break or go stale.
risks.mitigation: The rolling 28-day re-enrichment updates shard paths. On image error, refetch the shard (or /api/v1/items) and update the entry. Fall back to the header, then a generated placeholder. Never synthesize legacy filenames.

risks.risk: Scope creep (sync, PlayStation, IGDB, prices) delays the usable prototype.
risks.mitigation: Strict milestone gates with measurable acceptance. The post-prototype backlog (M6 sync, IGDB, ITAD after asking, Web Push release reminders) stays out of M0-M5.

why_this_wins:
1. Speed comes from the architecture.
   - The two hot paths, search and write, never touch the network.
   - Measured on this PC, the prefix index answers in 0-0.3 ms against a 50 ms budget. That is over 100x headroom, and still over 10x on phones that are several times slower.
   - Writes land in memory first and are persisted afterwards.
   - Offline is the normal state, not a special mode.
2. Operations are minimal.
   - No database server and no always-on backend to patch.
   - The catalog is a pure function of Steam data, rebuilt by a cron job into immutable static files.
   - If Steam, GitHub or the pipeline fail, clients keep working with their last snapshot.
   - Milestone 1 needs zero server code.
3. It costs €0/month on free tiers with wide headroom: static requests are unlimited, and the Worker is off the hot path.
4. Compliance is largely built in.
   - Until a user asks for Steam import or sync, we hold no personal data: no accounts, no cookies, no consent banner.
   - The Steam key exists only in two secret stores.
   - About 5 keyed calls/day against a cap of 100,000.
5. It withstands changes to Steam's APIs.
   - The only hard dependency is the documented, keyed GetAppList: 1 call/day plus 4 per week.
   - The undocumented endpoints only add enrichment and degrade gracefully.
   - Browsers never call Steam, so the missing CORS headers do not matter.
6. It suits a solo developer on this machine.
   - One language (TypeScript) for app, worker, pipeline and API.
   - One shared library for normalization and ranking, tested once.
   - Runs on the installed Node 24 + npm + git, with no Docker, Python or Postgres.
7. It can evolve.
   - UUIDs, per-field HLC stamps and an outbox make sync an addition rather than a rewrite.
   - The catalog layer is source-agnostic, ready for IGDB or PlayStation later.
   - The same PWA can be wrapped with Tauri 2 or Capacitor 8.5 if store presence is ever needed.
honest_weaknesses:
- First visit:
  - It downloads about 2.0-2.4 MB.
  - On slow networks, Steam search needs a few seconds after first load; manual add and link paste work immediately.
  - Users on capped mobile data may notice it.
- Freshness:
  - The catalog is daily at best, because the GitHub cron is best-effort.
  - A game announced today is not searchable until the next run. Workarounds: link paste and manual add, then the M4 API lookup.
- No sync in the prototype:
  - Data lives in one browser profile per device.
  - Safari can delete non-installed sites after 7 days. Export/import is a stopgap until M6.
- iOS is second-class:
  - No Web Share Target, installation by hand, and the Home Screen app's storage is separate from Safari's.
  - With no Mac, Safari can only be checked via Playwright WebKit on Windows and the in-app perf panel.
- Undocumented endpoints:
  - Everything beyond names depends on them: Spanish names, covers, flags, popularity.
  - If they break, the app degrades to names-only search until fixed.
- Memory:
  - The search worker holds about 20-30 MB.
  - Very low-end phones may kill it in the background, costing a 1-3 s rebuild on resume.
- Covers:
  - Hotlinking sends users' IPs to Valve. This is disclosed and can be switched off.
  - Images are full-size 600x900 JPEGs, because there is no free resizing.
- Missing games: games delisted before our first snapshot are not in the catalog (GetAppList excludes them) and must be added manually.
- Steam only:
  - The prototype catalog covers Steam alone.
  - PlayStation 'platinado' is a manual flag.
  - No multi-platform metadata until IGDB arrives.
- No reminders: release-day reminders need Web Push (iOS 16.4+ for installed apps) plus a push backend that stores subscriptions, which are personal data. Out of scope.
- Search:
  - M1 ranking has no popularity signal; it arrives in M2.
  - No typo tolerance until it proves necessary.
